en: Thus have I heard— Dīgha Nikāya 7: The Jāliya Sutta.
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Kosambī in Ghosita’s Park.
Now at that time two wanderers, Muṇḍiya the Paribbājaka and Jāliya the pupil of Dārupattika, approached the Blessed One; having approached, they exchanged greetings with the Blessed One.
Having exchanged greetings and pleasantries, they stood to one side. Standing there, those two wanderers said this to the Blessed One:
"Friend Gotama, is the soul the same as the body, or is the soul one thing and the body another?
"In that case, friends, listen and pay close attention; I shall speak."
“Yes, friend,” those two wanderers replied to the Blessed One.
The Blessed One said this:
“In this case, friends, a Tathāgata arises in the world, an Arahant, a Perfectly Enlightened One … [as before] …”
In this way, friends, a bhikkhu is accomplished in virtue.
…pe… Having attained the first jhāna, he dwells therein.
"Friend, for a bhikkhu who knows thus and sees thus, would it be appropriate for him to say,
'The soul is the same as the body,' or 'The soul is one thing and the body another'?
"Friend, for a bhikkhu who knows thus and sees thus, it would indeed be appropriate for him to say that."
‘That which is the soul is the body,’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another.

Yet, friend, this is how I know and how I see; nevertheless, I do not say: [that the Tathāgata exists after death... [or that he does not exist... [or that he both exists and does not exist... [or that he neither exists nor does not exist after death].”
‘That which is the soul is the body,’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ …pe… the second jhāna … the third jhāna …
He enters and dwells in the fourth jhāna.
Friend, for a bhikkhu who thus knows and thus sees, would it be appropriate for him to say,
‘The soul and the body are the same,’ or ‘The soul is one thing and the body another’?
"Friends, for a bhikkhu who thus knows and thus sees, it is appropriate to say either,
'The soul is the same as the body,' or 'The soul is one thing and the body another.
But I, friends, know and see it in this way."
And yet, I do not say:
"The soul is the same as the body," nor do I say: "The soul is one thing and the body another"... [and so on]...
he directs and inclines his mind toward the attainment of knowledge and vision.
"Friend, for a bhikkhu who knows thus and sees thus, would it be appropriate for him to say,
'The soul is the same as the body,' or 'The soul is one thing and the body another'?
"Friend, for a bhikkhu who knows thus and sees thus, it would indeed be appropriate for him to say that."
‘That which is the soul is the body,’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another.
Yet, friend, this is how I know and how I see;
nevertheless, I do not say:
‘That which is the soul is the body,’ or ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’ … [as before] … He understands:
‘There is no further state of being.
Friend, is it appropriate for a bhikkhu who knows thus and sees thus to say: [that the world is eternal, etc.]?
“Is it that ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or that ‘the soul is one thing and the body another’?
“Friend, for a bhikkhu who knows thus and sees thus,
it is not appropriate to say either that ‘the soul is the same as the body’ or that ‘the soul is one thing and the body another.’”
"However, friend, I know this and I see this;
yet I do not say:
'the soul is the same as the body,' nor do I say: 'the soul is one thing and the body another.'"
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Those two wanderers, being uplifted in mind, rejoiced in the words of the Blessed One.
The Jāliya Sutta, the seventh, is concluded.
